title: The tune 'Mr. Jones' and Elvin's 3/4 playing
summary: He wrote 'Mr. Jones' in 3/4 out of his admiration for Elvin's playing with Coltrane.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Yeah. Probably got surrounded there. Just to go back to the composing for a bit, you have a tune that you wrote called “Mr. Jones” I believe. And was there a reason that you chose, I think it’s either 6/8 or 3/4 groove. Is there a reason for that?

Well I love Elvin’s playing on 3/4. If you listen to him on recordings with John, there’s one that they do called “Spiritual,” which is in C minor. So really that feeling of what we’re playing is kind of loosely, in my humble ability, to try to come from that spirit or the energy that John Coltrane played from. “Live at the Vanguard” is our spiritual, is our spirit, which as a group is from that. So it is my appreciation for Elvin’s ability to play in 3/4.
